title: Readers’ Rides: Pierre’s Raleigh Royal Custom
content:
Pierre from Bike Felix sent in a wonderful Readers’ Rides submission of his Raleigh Royal Custom. Let’s check it out!

I always wanted to have only one bike; I love bikes too much to allow myself to own too many. But having one single bike is truly a hard thing to achieve, as cycling has so much to offer and each bike can really bring out a whole different experience.

This was my brief when I started to build this bike almost 5 years ago now. Back then I was hunting for a vintage touring frame build with reputable tubing and with more clearance than the usual 25/28c found on most vintage bikes. The candidate ended up being this lovely Raleigh Royal from 1988. I bought the frame and started my hunt for the parts.

The build took a long time. I wanted every part to be right and for once I didn’t want to do a period correct restoration but bring a few exotic components. I transferred most of the parts from my previous iteration of the “perfect bike”, a Peugeot PF10 which ended up being too roadie for my taste.

I wanted to keep a classic look while using some modern components. By modern, I mean components still available new today. Do not expect any Shimano DI2 or any other bulky all-black derailleur here. I went all silver and polished, not only because, to me, it looks gorgeous, but in my experience it is also easier to clean.

The transmission uses a Sugino PX crankset with my favourite BCD the 50.4. Gearing-wise, it is a 2×10 with a 42-26T at the front and an 11-32T cassette on the back. I always get confused with gear ratios, so I just tried a few different combinations until this one, which feels right. The shifting is operated with Simplex retroshifters, still my favourite friction shifters to this day, and they are mounted on Gevenalle Gran Compe brake levers. The derailleurs are Microshift R10, picked because they are polished and kinda look classic.

Wheels were hand-built by VeloDuo (a UK bike shop), and I had to go for high flanges for the look; the hubs are Sun XCD with Velo Orange rims. And tyres are Fairweather For CX in that lovely green colour, and obviously tanwall!

The handlebar is a lovely Nitto B135 AA Randonneur, super comfy and slightly flared, and the bar tape is Ergon, matching the tire color perfectly. I also added a front and rear rack for when I go on longer rides and need to carry more stuff; the front is a BLB and the rear is a Nitto R10. There are a lot of smaller cool parts, such as the VO Modernist bottle cages or the MKS Gordito pedals, but I will list the tech specs at the end so you can deep dive into every component.

This bike gets ridden all around the UK; it’s my go-to adventure bike, whether it’s a day ride in the forest, a small bikepacking trip, or even a city ride to the other end of London. I’ve been on many New Forest trips, and with those new gravel tires it really handles more serious gravel than before. I love this bike, my only wish would be bigger tyres, but maybe one day I will convert it to 650B who knows!

Here is the full spec sheet for those who care about this…

Build Spec:

Tubing: Full Reynolds 531 ST
Transmission: Microshift R10
Brake/Shifters: Gevenalle Gran Compe with Simplex retroflection shifters
Brake Calipers: Dia Compe DC980
Crankset: Sugino PX with Specialites TA 26-42
Wheels: Custom-made High Flange SunXCD MK2 Hubs with Velo Orange Enterprise 32H rim
Tyres: Fairweather for CX 700x32c
Cassette: Shimano 10-speed 11-32T
Saddle: Brooks Cambium C17 Carved
Seatpost: Fluted unbranded
Headset: Tange Levin CD
Stem: Nitto Technomic
Handlebar: Nitto B135 AA Randonneur – 450mm
Bartape: Ergon BT Gravel
Bottom bracket: Shimano UN55
Pedals: MKS Gordito
Chain: KMC 10 Speed
Bottle Cages: VO Modernist
Front Rack: BLB
Rear rack: Nitto R10
Cable housing: Nissen

 

 

We’d like to thank all of you who submitted Readers Rides builds to be shared here at The Radavist. The response has been incredible, and we have so many to share over the next few months.
